title: Delivering Bad News
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Dar malas noticias es la prueba de fuego de cualquier líder corporativo. Al usar estas estructuras de amortiguación (buffering) y vocabulario avanzado, puedes mantener la calma y el respeto incluso en las peores crisis.

parts.visual:
En los negocios, rara vez se dicen las malas noticias de golpe. Usamos una técnica de 'amortiguación' (Buffering) y frases formales. 

1. I regret to inform you (Lamento informarle): 
- La forma más clásica y profesional de empezar una mala noticia escrita. 
Ej: I REGRET TO INFORM YOU that your application was unsuccessful. 

2. We are forced to / We have no choice but to (Nos vemos obligados a): 
- Desplaza la culpa a las circunstancias externas. 
Ej: Due to the recession, WE ARE FORCED TO close the branch. 

3. Shortfall / Setback (Déficit / Contratiempo): 
- Suavizar palabras como 'fracaso' o 'pérdida'. 
Ej: We experienced a significant SHORTFALL in revenue this quarter.
parts.audio: Welcome to Delivering Bad News. In business, we rarely deliver bad news bluntly. We use a buffering technique and highly formal phrases. Number 1: I regret to inform you. This is the most classic and professional way to start a written bad news message. For example: I REGRET TO INFORM YOU that your application was unsuccessful. Number 2: We are forced to, or We have no choice but to. This shifts the blame to external circumstances. For example: Due to the recession, WE ARE FORCED TO close the branch. Number 3: Shortfall or Setback. These are nouns used to soften harsh words like failure or loss. For example: We experienced a significant SHORTFALL in revenue this quarter.

parts.visual:
4. Unfortunately / Regrettably (Desafortunadamente / Lamentablemente): 
- Adverbios esenciales para iniciar una oración negativa en persona. 
Ej: REGRETTABLY, we cannot offer you the position. 

5. It has come to my attention (Ha llegado a mi conocimiento): 
- Una forma diplomática pero firme de confrontar a alguien por un error. 
Ej: IT HAS COME TO MY ATTENTION that the reports are constantly late. 

6. Fall short of (No alcanzar / Quedarse corto): 
- Eufemismo para decir que algo fracasó o no cumplió la meta. 
Ej: The marketing campaign FELL SHORT OF our expectations.
parts.audio: Number 4: Unfortunately, or Regrettably. These adverbs are essential to start a negative sentence in person. For example: REGRETTABLY, we cannot offer you the position. Number 5: It has come to my attention. This is a diplomatic but very firm way to confront someone about an error or bad behavior. For example: IT HAS COME TO MY ATTENTION that the reports are constantly late. Number 6: Fall short of. This is a common euphemism used to say that something failed or didn't meet the goal. For example: The marketing campaign FELL SHORT OF our expectations.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la expresión correcta para dar malas noticias.

questions.question: Dear Mr. Smith, I ____ to inform you that we have chosen another candidate for the role.
questions.explanation: I regret to inform you = Lamento informarle (muy formal).

questions.question: Due to the sudden increase in taxes, we have no ____ but to raise our prices.
questions.explanation: We have no choice but to = No tenemos más remedio que.

questions.question: Instead of saying 'We lost money', the report said: 'We experienced a massive financial ____.'
____, we will not be able to attend the conference this year. (Lamentablemente).
It has ____ to my attention that some employees are arriving late. (Me he enterado / Me han informado).
questions.explanation: It has come to my attention = ha llegado a mi conocimiento.

questions.question: The new product launch completely failed; it ____ short of all our expectations.
questions.explanation: Fall short of (pasado: fell short of) = no alcanzar, quedarse corto.

questions.question: We are ____ to announce the closure of our Madrid office. (Nos vemos obligados).
questions.explanation: We are forced to = nos vemos obligados a.

questions.question: This isn't a failure, it's just a temporary ____. We will recover next month. (Contratiempo).
I'm writing to ____ you that your account has been suspended. (Avisar/Notificar de forma dura).
questions.explanation: Advise = en inglés legal/formal significa notificar o informar (I advise you that...).

questions.question: I'm ____ that we cannot accept your proposal at this time. (Me temo).
questions.explanation: I'm afraid that = Me temo que (amortiguador clásico).

questions.question: We have carefully ____ your request, but we must decline it. (Considerado).
questions.explanation: Carefully considered = considerado cuidadosamente (para suavizar el rechazo).

questions.question: Due to circumstances ____ our control, the delivery will be delayed. (Fuera de).
questions.explanation: Circumstances beyond our control = circunstancias ajenas/fuera de nuestro control.

questions.question: Please accept our sincere ____ for the inconvenience caused. (Disculpas).
We are writing to ____ you of a data breach affecting your account. (Notificar).
questions.explanation: Notify = notificar (verbo formal para alertas graves).

questions.question: This decision was not made ____. (A la ligera).
questions.explanation: Not made lightly = no se tomó a la ligera (para dar gravedad a la mala noticia).

questions.question: The board has ____ the difficult decision to restructure the company. (Tomado).
questions.explanation: Take a decision (o Make a decision) = tomar una decisión.

questions.question: I have some ____ news regarding the Q3 financial results. (Noticias difíciles).
questions.explanation: Tough news = noticias difíciles o malas.

questions.question: We must ____ the fact that the project is no longer viable. (Afrontar).
questions.explanation: Face the fact = afrontar el hecho.

questions.question: There's no easy way to ____ this, but we are letting you go. (Decir/Expresar).
questions.explanation: No easy way to say this = no hay forma fácil de decir esto.

questions.question: We understand this is ____ news, and we are here to support you. (Decepcionante).

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra clave de comunicación formal.

questions.question: I ____ to inform you... (Lamento con R)
We have no ____ but to... (Opción/Remedio con C)
A financial ____. (Déficit con S)
____, we must decline. (Lamentablemente con R)
It has ____ to my attention. (Llegado con C)
It fell ____ of our expectations. (Corto con S)
We are ____ to close it. (Obligados con F)
A temporary ____. (Contratiempo con S)
Circumstances ____ our control. (Fuera de / Más allá de con B)
Sincere ____. (Disculpas con A)
